bibliographic.title: A data-driven governance framework for co-creation healthcare quality in public hospitals
bibliographic.citation_apa: Dang, H. P., & Vo, N.-K.-T. (2026). A data-driven governance framework for co-creation healthcare quality in public hospitals. Discover Public Health, 23, 1087. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12982-026-02342-x

methodology.method_family: exploratory mixed-methods combining conceptual governance framework with computational text analytics (BERTopic topic modelling and prompt-based LLM aspect-based sentiment analysis)
methodology.study_design: exploratory mixed-methods design with single-site secondary data analysis of public patient reviews
methodology.sample_description: 450 publicly available patient reviews from Google Maps (Q4 2024–Q3 2025) for one public hospital in Viet Nam
methodology.technology_context: Gemini 1.5 Flash used for prompt-based ABSA with controlled prompting, JSON-constrained outputs, and automated retry mechanisms; BERTopic with PhoBERT embeddings, UMAP, and HDBSCAN for topic modelling

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article clearly addresses data-driven healthcare quality governance in public hospitals and empirically uses a specific LLM (Gemini 1.5 Flash) for ABSA on patient reviews, aligning with regulated healthcare and governance themes. However, the provided text does not examine conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, guardrails, human oversight of interactive LLM systems, or governance of LLM-based conversational deployments; the LLM functions as an analytic extraction tool within a public-health intelligence pipeline.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Automated triage scored the paper as a central candidate due to strong governance, healthcare, and LLM term overlap, but full-text signals indicate governance of healthcare quality rather than conversational governance of LLM systems.

appraisal.notes: Objectives and mixed-methods design are clearly stated and methodologically coherent for exploratory PX analytics. Sampling is transparent but single-site and context-specific. LLM use is described with prompting and output constraints, yet the text provided does not appraise LLM accountability, safety governance, or oversight mechanisms for the model itself.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are internally coherent for translating patient reviews into governance-relevant quality signals, but relevance to conversational LLM governance is low because the study does not analyze interactive conversational systems or their governance controls.

axial_codes: operational quality signals from unstructured reviews
coding.theme: Data-driven governance of healthcare quality using patient review analytics
coding.subtheme: LLM-supported ABSA for governance-relevant PX signals in public hospitals

synthesis.main_claim: Patient reviews can be converted into structured, interpretable, governance-relevant healthcare quality signals through topic modelling and LLM-based ABSA, supporting data-informed governance in public hospitals.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes and empirically illustrates a data-driven governance framework that reframes patient-generated data as inputs for healthcare quality monitoring and priority-setting in a public hospital setting.
synthesis.limitations: Exploratory, context-specific findings from one Vietnamese public hospital; the study does not directly examine governance processes or decision-making and does not address governance of conversational LLM systems.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as borderline or peripheral evidence on LLM use for analytics in regulated healthcare governance; not suitable as central evidence on conversational governance of LLM-based interactive systems unless the review scope is broadened beyond conversational AI.
